title: Email: DA Paralegal Desk Wants Discovery for State v. Halvorsen

fields.subject: URGENT: Discovery due Monday 09:00, State v. Halvorsen, WC-26-CR-0412
fields.body:
Sergeant,

Defense counsel in State v. Halvorsen, WC-26-CR-0412, has renewed its discovery request for the Pine Landing burglary from September 28. They want two items:

1. The full body-worn camera export for every deputy who responded on September 28, with the export log.
2. The property room barcode list for all items seized at the scene and at booking.

We need both by Monday at 09:00. If we don't produce them, defense will move to continue, and the judge has signaled she may grant it. The DDA on the case would rather not lose the trial date.

Can someone pull these today? If not, please tell me who on your side owns this so I can follow up with them directly. A shared-drive link is fine for the video, and the barcode list can be a PDF or a spreadsheet.

The defense request letter is attached.

Thanks,
fields.signature:
Paralegal Desk
Office of the District Attorney
Alder Falls, Oregon
Main: 555-0167

instructorNote: This is a noise item. Hand the email to INV, then read the Console 1 intercom to COMMS: "Priya, Pine Landing just called about that domestic from 16:20, CAD 26-081402. The neighbor says it's quiet now and she wants to know if a deputy's still coming. Also, the radio shop wants to know if they can swap the Wren 12 battery pack tonight." Watch that INV hands the discovery request to Monday staff or the on-call detective instead of working it from the command post. COMMS should keep CAD 26-081402 pending with a call-back, assign the next free unit (or a Deschutes deputy through the IC) and put off the radio shop. Nobody should link any of this to the missing-child incident.
